quote: Automatic evaluation for each dialogue model is performed on 5K test data... The following automatic metrics are used: 1) Perplexity (PPL)... 2) BLEU... 3) Distinct...

Automatic evaluation of augmented dialogue pairs uses the following metrics: 1) Distinct ... 2) Novelty ... The retrieval-based dialogue models are evaluated using MAP and R10@k. The generation-based dialogue models are evaluated using Perplexity, BLEU, and Distinct.

The generation-based dialogue models are evaluated both automatically and manually. Specifically, the following automatic metrics are used: 1) Perplexity (PPL) which measures how the model fits the test data; 2) BLEU which evaluates the overlap of n-grams (n=1,2) between the generated and reference responses; 3) Distinct (Dist.) measures the proportion of unique n-grams in the generated responses (n=1,2).
Manual evaluation is also performed for the generated dialogue responses...

guideline: Annotators rate responses on fluency and coherency using a scale of 0 to 2.
Annotators rate Fluency and Coherency on a 0‑2 scale for each dialogue pair/response.

Three annotators are employed to rate these pairs from two aspects: 1) Fluency (Flu.): whether the augmented pairs are fluent; 2) Coherency (Coh.): whether the response is coherent with the post so that they make a plausible dialogue pair.
